fixture.source: paced deterministic PCM noise for progressive seek fixtures; original tone for local and ordinary queue modes
fixture.note: Loaded backward and nearby seeks pass on both revisions. Delay one old-playhead HTTP read to exercise seekable but unloaded targets on macOS without modifying player buffering.
fixture.latency: Two advancing 100 ms native-clock samples within 0.5 s of target, playing status, and agreeing exposed position; includes sampling overhead. Future target includes production wait plus buffering lead. Baseline hangs are right-censored at 12 s.

reliability_recheck.note: Original sources and queue modes unchanged. Historical second_track_gap_seconds is retained but uses exposed positions updated at 500 ms; native_second_track_gap_seconds uses advancing native clocks, recalculated for both old and new telemetry. Jitter exposed-position gap increased from 0 to 0.244 s while native gap fell from 0.229 to 0.188 s. No repeat run or production fix was needed.

audible.note: Decoded PCM from a real AVPlayer audio tap; tolerance 1 s including capture latency and frequency quantization.

flac_mp4_regression.note: Final queue and seek-recheck oracles pass. Initial queue/recheck and all seek attempts are retained. The initial queue run under concurrent compilation flagged one exposed-clock update delay with a continuous native clock. seek_final flagged one playing old-clock sample 0.6 ms after command issue, before the unchanged async seek task paused; seek_initial and seek_recheck passed. No existing oracle was relaxed. Jitter wait distribution changes: fewer first-song wait seconds but a larger second-song gap; all queue completion times remain within 0.1 s of reliability_recheck. This is not a blanket no-timing-regression claim.
